Java 8 features: Lambda Expressions

A 'text-message shortcut' for code. Instead of writing long instructions for a robot to jump, you use a tiny arrow -> to say, 'Take this and do that!'

Java 8 features: Functional Interfaces

A toy with only one button. Because it has only one abstract method, Java knows exactly what to do when the Lambda shortcut is used.

Java 8 features: Streams

Like a conveyor belt for data. You can filter red bricks, map them into stars, and collect them in a bucket without touching each brick individually.
code:
List<String> bucket = bricks.stream()
    .filter(b -> b.getColor().equals("Red"))
    .map(b -> b.convertToStar())
    .collect(Collectors.toList());

Java 8 features: Optional

A clear plastic box used to prevent crashes. Instead of grabbing an empty toy box and 'crying' (NullPointerException), you check if the box has something first.

Java 8 features: Default Methods

The 'Main Blueprint' (Interface) upgrade. You can add a 'Dance' move to the blueprint so all 100 robots learn it instantly without changing each one.

Java 21 feature: Virtual Threads (The Tiny Army)

Instead of a few heavy, expensive robots, you have 10,000 tiny, lightweight sprites. If one sprite waits for paint to dry, it disappears and lets another take its place instantly.

Java 21 feature: Record Patterns (The Smart Sorter)

You don't have to manually 'open the box' to take out values. You can just say, 'If this is a Point box, give me the numbers inside it right now!'

Java 21 feature: Pattern Matching for Switch

The 'Super Scanner.' Instead of just checking for numbers or words, the switch can check for the type of object (Truck, Doll, Broken Toy) and handle them gracefully.

Java 21 feature: Sequenced Collections (The Neat Line)

Like putting all your toys on a string. Now there are dedicated buttons to grab the first toy, the last toy, or flip the whole line backwards without extra math.

Java 21 feature: String Templates (The Fill-in-the-Blanks)

Like a Mad Libs book. Instead of messy '+' signs to glue strings together, you just write a normal sentence and fill in the blanks using the \{name} syntax.

Java Multi-threading: The Helper

A Thread is like one friend helping you. Multi-threading is having a whole team of friends working together to finish tasks faster.

Java Multi-threading: Concurrency vs. Parallelism

Concurrency (The Busy Chef): One chef switching quickly between tasks on one stove. Parallelism (Many Chefs): Multiple chefs cooking on multiple stoves at the exact same second.
code:
// Concurrency is often achieved via Time Slicing on a single CPU core.
// Parallelism is achieved when multiple threads run on multiple CPU cores simultaneously.

body:
Java Multi-threading: Shared Resources (The Cookie Jar)

If two friends reach for the last cookie at once, they might 'bump heads.' In Java, this is a Race Condition where threads mess up the math by changing the same number simultaneously.

Java Multi-threading: Synchronized (The Bathroom Key)

To fix the cookie jar problem, use Synchronization. It's like a gas station bathroom key: only one person can hold the key (the Lock) and use the room at a time.

Java Multi-threading: Deadlock (The Grumpy Stand-off)

Friend A has the Milk but needs Cereal. Friend B has the Cereal but needs Milk. Neither will share, so they sit staring at each other forever, and the program 'freezes.'

Java Multi-threading: ExecutorService (The Manager)

Instead of calling friends individually, you hire a Manager. You give them a list of 100 tasks, and they hand them out to a Thread Pool (a group of friends sitting on a bench).
